items.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Interviewee mentions Ellington only as an example of an 'iconic situation' or 'major group' when asked by the interviewer: 'Are you speaking of people like Charles Mingus and Ellington?'

ctx.x: Well I might have been referring to how I have observed, you know, those few instances when a musician may have, by the way — not by what they say but by the way they perform when they’re playing with you that their minds and persona is not as a team player. You know. And in that case it would be better for them to do their own thing or go do it somewhere else. But generally — it really depends on the flavor and what is the aspirations of anyone that calls you for a gig or what you want to have happen, you know,…
Are you speaking of people like Charles Mingus and Ellington?

Oh absolutely. Absolutely. But also Max Roach and Clifford Brown. They created a repertory that will live forever, a repertory of using the Great American Songbook, as well as their own compositions, and putting arrangements to them that will last forever. I mean the show — Broadway writers had no idea that those beautiful songs that they wrote that became a part of the American Songbook could be completely made even better you know, with chord substitutions and rhythmical arrangements and rhythmical © Fillius…
